Guishan: phase 1 has 34 × 3 MW (93 MW connected by May 2019; three turbines with damaged foundations, 02#, 05# and 31#, were rebuilt in 2020). In June 2021 the “phase-1 follow-up and phase 2” design (the unbuilt 3 × 6 MW of phase 1 and 15 × 5.5 MW of phase 2) was changed to 7 × 6.45 MW and 8 × 7 MW (101.15 MW in all); 13 of them were connected when the farm reached full capacity in December 2021 (GlobalData: 5 Mingyang MySE6.45-180 and 8 Dongfang DEW-D7000-186), and two more on bucket foundations (the first set in June 2022, bucket works extended to May 2025; cables at turbines 35# and 43# re-laid in June 2024) were added in 2024. The Guangzhou MSA completion notice (July 2025) gives 49 turbines and 200 MW (approved capacity 198 MW; the design figures add up to 203.15 MW). The year stays 2021 (full capacity); the models and ratings of the two later units are not published

This is CGN's Xiangshan Tuci offshore wind farm (off Tuci, north-east of Xiangshan county, the same point as GEM's Xiangshan Tuci), not Guodian's Xiangshan 1 phase 1 (south-east of Hepu, already in GEM's Xiangshan 1); “Xiangshan 1 Phase 1” in the name was a mix-up. Phase 1 is connected (Ningbo Daily, July 2025), with CSSC Haizhuang 8 MW-class turbines (Hitachi Energy release, July 2022; broker report), not 'Mingyang 6.45 MW'. A sea-use change report written after the August 2022 adjustment approval says it was 'not yet in construction', so 2022 is wrong; a China Post Securities report (Oct 2023) lists “CGN Xiangshan Tuci 280 MW, connected in 2023” and GEM also gives 2023, so the year is 2023 (the owner's full-connection notice is unverified); a Ningbo MSA notice (Nov 2024) says it is “built and in use” with 38 × 8 MW (the earlier 35 turbines, 280 MW, predate the amendment)

CSSC Haizhuang's floating wind prototype (the 'offshore floating wind equipment test site' whose EIA was filed by Guangdong Haizhuang Offshore Wind Power Research Center), towed to the Luodousha waters off Qianshan, Xuwen and installed in late May 2022; it ran in intelligent-microgrid (off-grid) mode in August 2023, and no later report of a formal connection to the public grid was found. The position comes from MSA chart-correction notice 795/2026, in which a cable of about 25.9 km runs from a lone turbine at Luodousha to a turbine in the Wailuo farm area, matching the 25.77 km 35 kV cable to turbine no. 27 of Guangdong Energy's Wailuo phase 2 in the EIA approval; the notice does not name the unit. The EIA gives 5.95 MW; reports of the installed unit give 6.2 MW.

Thanh Hai No. 5 is four plants with 28 turbines (EVN, Jul 2022; the piling contractor Le Thy says 24, EVN is preferred).
